law: The browser dependency closure may only reach the outside world through these five service classes; each records today's native assumption, today's wasm32 seam, and the owning node for the real boundary.

services.nativeAssumption: ambient-library reads plus a filesystem-backed workspace
services.wasmRoute: host-provided in-memory virtual workspace (resolve/upsert/remove/listVirtualFiles); ambient-library reads are compiled out behind cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))
services.boundaryOwner: BWH2 (portable platform-services boundary); BWH4 (browser VFS and project snapshot adapter)

services.nativeAssumption: scheduler driver thread plus CPU/IO worker pools plus rayon batch compile
services.wasmRoute: sync inline drive (wait_or_drive drives stages inline); driver thread, blocking semaphore and rayon batch are compiled out on wasm32; no thread is available to an admitted portable operation
services.boundaryOwner: BWH2 (boundary); BWH5 (worker protocol, prioritization and the optional threaded strategy)

services.nativeAssumption: env-hash artifact stores and durable cache roots (FileArtifactStore)
services.wasmRoute: in-memory caches only; the browser closure has no durable artifact store
services.boundaryOwner: BWH8 (browser cache, artifact loading and offline integrity)

services.nativeAssumption: tsgo provider spawn through verter_type_runtime (tokio process), feature-gated and absent from the default closure
services.wasmRoute: none; the browser closure has no process capability; the only sanctioned browser-to-native route is the explicitly selected authenticated local companion (DX4/DX5)

environmentNotes: Randomness: getrandom uses the wasm_js backend (.cargo/config.toml) and uuid uses its js feature (WebCrypto) on wasm32; native uses rng-getrandom behind cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32")).
Allocator: the default Rust global allocator with console_error_panic_hook (verter_wasm default feature); no custom allocator is pinned.
rules: A service class may not gain a native assumption inside the browser closure; a new assumption is a receiving-owner amendment before code.
Threads, filesystem, processes and sockets are not available to admitted portable operations; reaching for one is a build blocker (BWH0-AC1), not a degraded mode.
Adapters inherit the DX0 receipt basis: reduced client capabilities preserve semantic meaning and create no background semantic work in closed views.
